title: Mint: Cost-Efficient Tracing with All Requests Collection via Commonality and Variability Analysis
problem: Distributed tracing systems face a fundamental tension between preserving essential trace information and reducing the massive volume of traces generated in production. The prevailing '1 or 0' binary sampling strategy either retains a full trace or discards it entirely, which fails to efficiently capture structural commonality across traces while still recording meaningful variability.
motivation: Real-world production traces show that most requests share structural patterns (commonality) while differing only in a small set of attributes (variability), making full retention wasteful and full discard lossy; a smarter representation can reduce cost without sacrificing observability.
method: Mint decomposes traces into a commonality skeleton shared across structurally similar requests and per-request variability deltas that capture deviations. It collects all requests but stores only the variability delta relative to the common template, reducing storage volume while preserving full per-request observability. A commonality and variability analysis pass extracts templates offline or incrementally from the trace stream.
key_novelty: Replacing binary trace sampling with a commonality-variability decomposition that retains full-request coverage at drastically reduced storage cost.
contributions: Empirical study revealing that real-world production traces exhibit strong commonality that binary sampling fails to exploit.
Mint's commonality and variability decomposition framework that achieves all-request collection at reduced cost.
Evaluation on real-world production trace workloads demonstrating cost-efficiency gains.
limitations: Not discussed; overhead of online commonality analysis and potential latency impact on traced services is not addressed in the abstract.
primary_theme: All-requests distributed tracing via commonality-variability decomposition
